newsitem.title: USA: AOL makes Excite exclusive directory.
newsitem.headline: AOL makes Excite exclusive directory.

text.p: America Online Inc and Excite Inc said Monday they had agreed to a deal to make Excite the exclusive Internet search and directory service for America Online's more than 7 million subscribers.

In addition, they said Excite will acquire AOL's WebCrawler search and directory service for about two million shares of Excite, raising AOL's ownership of Excite to approximately 20 percent from its current 10 percent level.
Through the partnership, the companies will also explore ways to better integrate "smart search" capabilities throughout America Online's information channels.
These "smart search" capabilities will will allow AOL users to search through AOL content more quickly and efficiently, a spokesman said.
By acquiring WebCrawler and becoming the exclusive Internet content search and directory service for AOL, Excite's traffic and users is expected to increase significantly.
AOL and Excite said this will enable them to create a powerful medium for advertisers and merchants.

The combined audiences of the two directories will create the most widely used Internet search directory on the Web, outpacing Yahoo, now the most popular, based on statistics the companies cited from market research firm PC-Meter.

Executives of the two firms said they expect the Excite search and directory service on AOL will become a primary venue for advertising and transactions, permitting advertisers to reach a broad audience through a single media buy.
All advertising appearing on the AOL search feature using Excite's search technology will be sald by AOL's Interactive Advertising group, with revenues split by AOL and Excite.

The additional audience that will accrue to the new search and directory service should result in additional advertising revenues for both companies, and further AOL's goal of diversifying its revenue base, AOL said.
Under the terms of the deal, AOL has been granted a seat on Excite's board of directors which will be filled by Steve Case, the chairman and chief executive of America Online.
At the same time, Bob Pittman, who was an independent director on the Excite board prior to joining AOL as president and chief executive of its AOL Networks unit, has resigned from the board.

They said the Webcrawler purchase is expected to be completed in early 1997, subject to several closing conditions, including due diligence and regulatory approvals. The deal will be accounted for as a purchase by Excite.
Excite shares swelled 1-7/8 to 8 in early trading Monday. America Online shares rose 1 to 32.
